**C1 — no; DISPUTABLE: part.** “A space is a custom experience you create inside Muse by describing your idea”. [Spaces announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/11/introducing-spaces-customize-muse-app/). Searched spaces, side chats, business features, skills, and architecture for organizational or work-area units. Spaces are customizable interfaces; no agent or role membership is defined. Treating the example business hubs as informal work areas supports **part**.

**C2 — no; DISPUTABLE: part.** [quotation withheld: muse.ai page] [Product design, system-prompt excerpt](https://muse.ai/blog/how-we-designed-muse). Searched for unit responsibilities and independently defined positions; neither was found for an area under C1. The quoted agent-level purpose could support **part** under the per-agent-charter provision.

**C3 — no; DISPUTABLE: part.** “You can see the full list of available connectors in your Muse app settings”. [Small-business announcement](https://about.fb.com/news/2026/09/introducing-muse-small-business/). Searched connector lists, skills, account records, and architecture for recorded owners or accountable parties. No such mapping was described. Interpreting named service connectors as provider records supports **part**.

**C4 — part.** [quotation withheld: muse.ai page]. [Safety design, Browser section](https://muse.ai/blog/security-and-safety-for-ai-agents-our-approach-with-muse). Describes internal assignment to a specialized agent. No runtime capability lookup available to any agent was found.
